title: EnsembleRetriever: arank_fusion uses different normalization logic than rank_fusion causing ValidationError in async
author: AliMuhammadAslam

comments.author: AliMuhammadAslam
comments.body:
I tracked this down to `arank_fusion` in `ensemble.py` using `not isinstance(doc, Document)` as its wrapping condition while `rank_fusion` uses `isinstance(doc, str)`. The one-line fix is to bring `arank_fusion` in line with the sync path.

I've already opened a PR with the fix and tests: #37737

Happy to take this one if a maintainer can assign it to me.

comments.author: AliMuhammadAslam
comments.body:
To add more detail on the approach:

The divergence lives in two spots inside `libs/langchain/langchain_classic/retrievers/ensemble.py`:

`rank_fusion` (lines 251-255):
```python
retriever_docs[i] = [
    Document(page_content=cast("str", doc)) if isinstance(doc, str) else doc  # type: ignore[unreachable]
    for doc in retriever_docs[i]
]
```

`arank_fusion` (lines 295-299):
```python
retriever_docs[i] = [
    Document(page_content=doc) if not isinstance(doc, Document) else doc
    for doc in retriever_docs[i]
]
```

The `# type: ignore[unreachable]` on the sync path shows this normalization is considered dead code for well-typed retrievers — but it exists as a safety net for bare strings. The async version should have the identical safety net. The fix is changing the single line in `arank_fusion` to use `isinstance(doc, str)` instead of `not isinstance(doc, Document)`.

PR #37737 has the one-line fix plus three unit tests covering: bare strings in sync, bare strings in async, and result consistency between the two paths.

comments.author: sanidhyasin
comments.body:
I'd like to work on this.

**Root cause:** `rank_fusion` wraps stray values with `Document(page_content=cast("str", doc)) if isinstance(doc, str) else doc`, but `arank_fusion` uses `Document(page_content=doc) if not isinstance(doc, Document) else doc`. So in the async path any non-`Document` (e.g. an `int`) gets passed as `page_content`, which fails Pydantic validation — whereas the sync path leaves it untouched.

**Proposed fix:** align `arank_fusion`'s check with `rank_fusion` (`isinstance(doc, str)`) so both paths behave identically, and add an async test mirroring the sync one.

@ccurme @mdrxy could you assign this to me? Thanks!

comments.body:
## Proposed fix

The divergence between  (sync) and  (async) is a one-line difference in the normalization guard:

| method | current guard | problem |
|---|---|---|
| `rank_fusion` | `isinstance(doc, str)` | wraps bare strings; everything else passes through |
| `arank_fusion` | `not isinstance(doc, Document)` | tries `Document(page_content=<value>)` for **any** non-Document — raises `pydantic_core.ValidationError` for non-string types |

**Fix:** change the async guard to match the sync guard:

```python
# Before (arank_fusion, line 297)
Document(page_content=doc) if not isinstance(doc, Document) else doc

# After
Document(page_content=cast("str", doc)) if isinstance(doc, str) else doc  # type: ignore[unreachable]
```

This is a minimal, focused change — one character class check in a single comprehension. The `cast` and `# type: ignore` comment already exist on the sync side so the style is consistent. No behaviour change for well-behaved retrievers that return `Document` objects.

I have a PR ready: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/37932 (currently auto-closed pending assignment). Happy to address any review feedback.
